reason: The episode ran runClient on Fabric and NeoForge and proved the LOD path from the game log and a PrintWindow capture. The steps (session.lock, latest.log location, NUL bytes in logs, JVM sweep) were learned the hard way and are not in one place; no skill covers dev-client runs.

A second run overwrote the log the assistant was reading; the skill says to read the run dir log but does not warn that a new run replaces it. The Fabric pack check read the real instance log instead, and the skill should say so.

The clouds rule was added this episode, but the procedure for setting it was not: NeoForge's options.txt had the key, Fabric's did not, so sed silently did nothing and the agent had to append by hand. The next session needs both branches written down.
Comparing four detail settings was only valid because each capture waited for the stat line to settle; this is the repeatable procedure for any setting sweep on a dev client.

A kill during an options save silently dropped settings in the NeoForge run dir; the next session would otherwise start with clouds or other settings reset and not notice. Records the check to run after a kill.

Background launch reported exit 127 twice; the game was actually running and the agent almost relaunched into a locked world. A durable check (log timestamp before relaunch) prevents a double client and a session lock conflict.

This run captured a screenshot after the Fabric background launch reported failed (exit 127), then committed a fix claimed as verified from that capture. The launch never ran the new jar, so the claim was unsupported. The rule needs to sit at the capture step, where the agent acts.

A `/tp` silently failed during this episode: the capture showed a different place than the one under test, and the stale view was only caught by eye. The success line in the log is the proof to check before any measurement.

The NeoForge run dir's options.txt lost its version line after a kill; the game then dropped every key binding. The skill covers truncation generally but not the version line or the key-binding consequence.
Clicking from a downscaled screenshot needs the display factor; this is a repeatable technique in the dev-client UI check and was used without being written down.
The graceful close lets the game write its settings; a hard kill during the save truncates options.txt. The skill says to stop and sweep but not how to stop the client safely.

In this episode the client-mode check depended on whether the per-server store was wiped before the run, and the vanilla server was stopped by command-line match. Neither procedure is in the skill yet; both were needed to read the logs correctly.

A dev run changed extend_dimension_fog with sed and relaunched; the settings state carried over between runs, so the next test inherited a changed value. The fix is to reset the setting and read back the loaded-settings line of the new launch.

A settings-row label rendered its caption twice; the bug was only caught by reading the full-resolution capture, and the fix needed a relaunch to confirm. The dev-client procedure has no settings-screen check yet.
Two loaders log the same message with different prefixes, so a prefix-anchored grep reports no reply on one of them. The store-move check needs an explicit before/after count to prove persistence.

Several working steps this episode were not in the skill: a night capture via /time, cropping a 3866px capture before reading it (Read downscales to 2000px), lowering renderDistance for a fast LOD check and restoring it, and the debug-levels on/off pair. Each one was needed and each was improvised.

The episode judged the noise-preview horizon by cropping a band from the full-resolution PrintWindow captures (preview on vs off) instead of reading the downscaled full frame. This is a reusable technique for this skill's screenshot checks and belongs in its screenshot bullet.
The episode waited for the game to load with a bounded log loop that also exits on a crash, a reusable pattern for dev client runs that the skill does not describe.

The episode lost two dig-and-capture rounds to a repro that missed its target, and the agent only found out from the screenshots. A rule to check the loaded extent and the fill lines first would have saved both.
The village check needed a locate-then-view-from-afar recipe; without it the real chunks load over the preview and the check shows nothing.
